title: The chart theming bridge resolves colour but not typography, so marks cannot measure text
foundBy: an agent hand-drawing charts against the useChartTheme bridge on 0.2.0, relayed by the repository owner
details:
`patterns/Chart.md` states that the kit ships no chart primitives, only a theming bridge: draw the marks yourself and take every value from `useChartTheme()`. The reason given is that d3 and canvas need concrete values such as `#1ee0ca` rather than `var(--color-accent)`.

That reasoning applies to type as much as to colour, and the bridge stops at colour. `ChartTheme` carries sixteen colour fields and no typography at all. There is no family, no size, no weight, and no way to ask how wide a string will render.

The kit already accepts that chart consumers need this. There is a dedicated `--font-size-chart-axis` token, and `styleAxis()` applies it along with `--font-family-mono` to axis text. It passes them as `var(...)` strings, which works for SVG and DOM text and is unusable for the two things a drawing consumer needs. `ctx.font` will not accept a `var()` string, and nothing can be laid out around text whose width is unknown.

Measurement is the part that bites. Any chart drawing a labelled box, a legend chip or a truncated tick has to know the label width before it draws. With no way to ask, a consumer either reimplements a twenty-line probe or hard-codes a per-character estimate. The estimate is what ships, because it is one line and looks right on the strings it was tested against. It is a design token copied into a magic number, so it rots silently when the type scale moves. The reporter estimated 7.4px per character against a real 8.39px and drew labels wider than the boxes around them.

The proposal is to extend the existing bridge with a resolved `fontFamily`, a resolved `fontSizeAxis` in pixels, and a `measureText` helper backed by a cached canvas context. Two details matter: invalidate the cached font on a theme flip, the same way colours are re-read, and account for web fonts settling after `document.fonts.ready`.

Worked around in the consuming app with the per-character estimate described above.

notes.text: Confirmed: ChartTheme at src/lib/chartTheme.ts:7-24 is sixteen colour fields with no typography, and styleAxis at chartTheme.ts:98-99 passes var(--font-family-mono) and var(--font-size-chart-axis) through as CSS strings.

The report names a companion useChartTheme and useTheme split-brain defect as filed separately. That report was not supplied, so nothing is recorded for it here. Ask the reporter for it before assuming this record covers it.

The repository owner adopted the stopping rule this branch had proposed and never had confirmed: fix the defects a consumer would hit, record everything else, and decide the rest at 0.3.0. This record is one of the six that wait, because each adds or changes a public prop, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks that the design be settled before the code is written.

They are one conversation rather than six, and this is the order they unlock in: CUI-014 first, because whether navigation is a supported use decides CUI-011; then CUI-012, because the `storageKey` convention decides CUI-010; then CUI-009 and CUI-011 together, which are both about sizing to content; and CUI-013 last, which stands alone. The Tooltip and MarkdownMinimap changes that already landed belong in the same conversation.

The per-character estimate stays in the consuming app until then, at 7.4px against a real 8.39px, which is what draws labels wider than the boxes around them.
